standard_prerequisites.name: Witt groups and Witt sheaves of schemes
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a scheme S the Witt group W(S) is the monoid of isometry classes of symmetric bundles modulo metabolic ones, and the Witt sheaf on the site of smooth S-schemes is the Zariski sheaf associated with the presheaf X maps to W(X); the Lambda-linear version tensors with a subring Lambda of Q. The authors recall this at source lines 878-894 and both objects are retained in the material.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes both sides of the counted isomorphism: the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of S and the pushforward of the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of the characteristic-zero fibre S_Q.

standard_prerequisites.name: Balmer's Witt groups with support and their localization sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a closed pair (X,Z) there are triangulated Witt groups W^i(X,Z) fitting in the long exact localization sequence of Balmer-Witt theory, and for a closed subscheme Z of Spec Z with open complement U the sequence W^0(S,S_Z) to W^0(S) to W^0(S_U) to W^1(S,S_Z) is exact; the authors recall this at source lines 2499-2512 and cite Balmer, Witt cohomology (1.7 and Th. 1.6).
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the exact sequence whose middle map is the map of the counted proposition and reduces the claim to the vanishing of W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for odd primes p at source lines 2529-2544.

standard_prerequisites.name: Gersten-Witt spectral sequence and purity for Witt groups
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a regular scheme S with the dimension function delta = -codim there is a converging spectral sequence with E^1 terms W^{-i-j}(S_(x), {x}) over the points of prescribed delta-value, and purity (devissage) identifies W^{-i-j}(S_(x),{x}) with W(kappa(x)) when i+j is 0 mod 4 and with 0 otherwise; the authors cite Balmer-Walter (Th. 6.1) at source lines 2546-2564.
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes the E^1 page whose terms are 2-primary torsion in positive characteristic, which is the observation that finishes the counted proof.

core_obligations: Reduce the general statement for a Z[1/2]-scheme S to the assertion that the canonical map W(S)[1/2] to W(S_Q)[1/2] is an isomorphism for regular S (source lines 2521-2525).

Use Balmer's Witt groups with support and the long exact localization sequence for a closed subscheme Z of Spec Z with open complement U to get the exact sequence whose middle map is nu^* (source lines 2529-2535).
Pass to the filtered inductive limit over closed subschemes and use additivity to reduce to the vanishing of the triangular Witt group W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for every odd prime p (source lines 2536-2544).

Build the niveau/Gersten-Witt spectral sequence for W^{-i-j}(S,S_p) with E^1 terms W^{-i-j}(S_(x),{x}) and evaluate them by purity: W(kappa(x)) when i+j is 0 mod 4 and 0 otherwise (source lines 2546-2564).

Conclude that every surviving E^1 term is 2-primary torsion because the residue fields have positive characteristic, so the whole spectral sequence vanishes after inverting 2 (source lines 2565-2567).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the isomorphism W(S)[1/2] = W(S_Q)[1/2] for regular S.
Introduce Witt groups with support and the localization exact sequence.
Reduce to the vanishing of W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for odd primes p.
Build the Gersten-Witt spectral sequence and compute its E^1 terms by purity.
Kill the E^1 terms by inverting 2.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 13.2 at source lines 2513-2519, label prop:Witt_2inverted: for a Z[1/2]-scheme S and a subring Lambda of Q with 2 invertible, the canonical map from the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of S to the pushforward of the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of the characteristic-zero fibre is an isomorphism. The proof at source lines 2520-2568 is the Witt analogue of the paper's key lemma but is proved directly and not deduced from it: it reduces to regular S and to the map on Witt groups W(S)[1/2] to W(S_Q)[1/2], then uses Balmer's Witt groups with support and the long exact localization sequence of a closed pair to reduce the claim to the vanishing of W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for every odd prime p, and finally writes down the niveau/Gersten-Witt spectral sequence of W^{-i-j}(S,S_p) whose E^1 terms purity identifies with W(kappa(x)) when i+j is 0 mod 4 and with 0 otherwise. The non-routine step is the last one: those surviving E^1 terms are 2-primary torsion precisely because the residue fields have positive characteristic, so inverting 2 collapses the spectral sequence, and it is this observation, not the machinery itself, that decides the proposition. The argument is a self-contained appendix computation in which each tool is standard but the order and the reduction are specific, so the card is rated H2.
